notes: Full read done 17 July 2026. Direct reads across the indicators: Aim 1 and the Nature Networks and Naturfa 30by30 work map to SI1 and SI2; refreshed Section 6 guidance for public authorities and biodiversity in impact assessments map to SI3; peatland and woodland targets are framed explicitly for net zero, so they carry SI6; SUDS, urban green infrastructure and catchment approaches touch SI7 and SI8. Aim 6 (evidence and monitoring) is the one to watch for IEG: the plan commits to a monitoring framework tied to the Bill's statutory targets, which is the same measurement problem as SI1 resilience assessment via SoNaRR and DECCA. The Sustainable Farming Scheme minimum of 10 percent habitat management per farm is the main delivery lever behind the SI2 restoration rate. Open question: the plan was published while the Bill was awaiting Royal Assent, so the target regulations timetable (two years from assent) is the date to track.
summary: Published 27 March 2026: the updated national plan, structured around six strategic aims (protect and restore ecosystems; safeguard species; tackle pressures; governance and capacity; engagement; evidence and monitoring). It commits to halting and reversing biodiversity loss by 2030 and recovery by 2050, in line with the Global Biodiversity Framework. Hard numbers: peatland restoration tripled from 600 to 1,800 hectares a year, 45,000 hectares by 2050; a 21,500 hectare tree planting aspiration by 2030; and a 50 percent cut in new invasive non-native species establishments by 2030 against 2000 levels. It names the Environment (Principles, Governance and Biodiversity Targets) (Wales) Bill as the foundation, with statutory biodiversity target regulations due within two years of Royal Assent.
title: Nature Recovery Action Plan 2026: six aims, tripled peatland target, statutory biodiversity targets within two years of Royal Assent
